ukmt-grey-2018-01.title: Simplify
ukmt-grey-2018-01.body:
The top is $3\times2018$ and the bottom is $4\times2018$. Cancel the common factor 2018 to get $\frac34$.

**Answer: (E) $\frac34$**

ukmt-grey-2018-03.title: Opposite faces in a net
ukmt-grey-2018-03.body:
Opposite faces must have the same colour. In a net, in any straight strip of four squares, the first and third squares are opposite faces and so are the second and fourth. The two squares above and below the strip are also opposite faces.

- A: the strip is white, black, white, grey, so the second and fourth (black and grey) differ. Not possible.
- B: the strip is black, grey, black, grey; the first and third match, the second and fourth match, and the two white squares above and below the strip are opposite and match. Possible.
- C, D, E: in each one a pair of opposite squares in the strip has different colours (C: black and grey; D: black and grey; E: white and black).

So only net B works.

**Answer: (B)**

ukmt-grey-2018-05.title: Make $a$ big and $b$ small
ukmt-grey-2018-05.body:
$a-b$ is largest when $a$ is as large as possible and $b$ as small as possible: $a=10$ and $b=-5$. Then $a-b=10-(-5)=15$.

**Answer: (D) 15**

ukmt-grey-2018-07.title: Use the diameter
ukmt-grey-2018-07.body:
Each circle touches the top and bottom of the rectangle, so its diameter is 7 cm and its radius 3.5 cm. The left circle touches the left side, so its centre is 3.5 cm from the left; the right circle touches the right side so its centre is 3.5 cm from the right, i.e. 7.5 cm from the left. The distance between centres is $7.5-3.5=4$ cm (equivalently $11-7$).

**Answer: (E) 4 cm**

ukmt-grey-2018-21.title: Rearrange the dove into rectangles
ukmt-grey-2018-21.body:
Let each small square have side $x$ cm. Cutting the dove into pieces and moving the quarter-circle pieces to fill the gaps turns the dove into a square of side $2x$ (area $4x^2$), a rectangle $2x$ by $3x$ (area $6x^2$) and a rectangle $2x$ by $x$ (area $2x^2$). So the area is $12x^2=192$, giving $x^2=16$ and $x=4$ cm.

The flag is 6 squares by 4 squares: $24\text{ cm}\times16\text{ cm}$.

**Answer: (D)**

ukmt-grey-2018-21.title: Dove is half the flag
ukmt-grey-2018-21.body:
The pieces fit together so that the dove covers exactly 12 of the 24 grid squares' worth of area, i.e. half the flag. So the flag has area $2\times192=384\text{ cm}^2$. All the options have sides in the ratio $3:2$, so the sides are $3k$ and $2k$ with $6k^2=384$, $k=8$, giving $24\text{ cm}\times16\text{ cm}$.

**Answer: (D)**

ukmt-grey-2018-22.title: Three moves are enough
ukmt-grey-2018-22.body:
Reading the dominoes as (4,6), (3,1), (4,2), (3,4), (6,1), (2,6): the ends contain three 4s and three 6s, with the 3s, 1s and 2s each appearing twice. In a correct line the 3s, 1s and 2s must pair up, so one 4 and one 6 are left over for the two ends of the line. That is already the case, so the end dominoes need not move.

Swap the 3rd and 5th dominoes: (4,6), (3,1), (6,1), (3,4), (4,2), (2,6). Now the last three dominoes join correctly (4|4 and 2|2). Swap the 2nd and 3rd dominoes: (4,6), (6,1), (3,1), (3,4), ... so the first two join (6|6). Finally rotate the third domino to (1,3): it joins 1|1 and 3|3. So three moves suffice.

Two moves are not enough: the two 1s must become adjacent, which needs one domino with a 1 rotated and a swap, and the same is true for the two 3s, and these cannot all be done in two moves. So the smallest number is 3.

**Answer: (C) 3**

ukmt-grey-2018-25.title: Congruent triangles
ukmt-grey-2018-25.body:
Since $AB=BC$ and $LB=AK$, we get $LC=BK$, and as $KB=AC$ we have $LC=AC$. Join $K$ to $C$. Triangles $ACK$ and $LCK$ have $AK=KL$, $AC=LC$ and common side $KC$, so they are congruent and $\angle KAC=\angle CLK$.

Let $\angle LBK=x$. As $KL=LB$, $\angle BKL=x$, and by the exterior angle theorem $\angle KLC$ (the exterior angle of triangle $KLB$ at $L$) $=2x$. Hence $\angle KAC=2x$, and since $AB=BC$ the base angles satisfy $\angle ACB=\angle KAC=2x$.

In triangle $ABC$: $x+2x+2x=180^\circ$, so $x=36^\circ$.

**Answer: (A) $36^\circ$**
